posts.title: The Power of One Day
posts.description: Today is a day to do only what I want, only when I want. The world is my oyster, and I'm going to shuck it. My husband is away on a guys' weekend, so the cats and I have the whole place to ourselves. I'm trying to make the most of my limited time, so I'm going to be planning ahead. I've minimized my obligations and potential complications by: only eating safe food for days prior doing the full grocery run earlier in the week leaving myself a single task that guarantees I leave the house After all, I know who I am as a person. I've played a video game straight through from start to finish in a single sitting instead of sleeping before. I may hate commitment, but I need some semblance of structure to not lose all track of time. I've even gone one step further: I planned my Saturday morning activities the night before. posts.title: Allowing Myself to Acknowledge Growth
posts.description: I don't know whether this is a universal experience, something unique to my life, or if the reality of it lands somewhere in the middle, but I feel as if nothing in life is truly constant. Before you get up in arms at the thought that I'm implying no one can have a loving relationship that lasts or a relatively consistently happy life, take a breath. What I mean to say is much more nuanced, and not in the, "Everything is stable and great until it's not," kinda way. I don't have any plans to pull the rug out from under you (or myself) in this post. In two separate blogs, Staying Sane and Maintaining Motivation and its follow up , I break down my thought process and progress with a motivation system I've developed to "earn" weed. posts.title: Rocking Chair Regrets
posts.description: Last month, I watched the Mythical Kitchen episode of Last Meals with Jennette McCurdy. I don't watch this series particularly often even though I feel they have a lot of celebrities I like. I'm really hit or miss on YouTube content, especially long-form videos, which is a fun and funny thing to think about when I used to make some longer content as well. I'm glad I made the time for this one, though. Of the many topics they discussed, one of the things she touched on was rocking chair regrets . I'd never heard of the concept before, but it's totally uprooted how I think about my time. I already have a bucket list, so it's not like mortality is a subject I tend to avoid thinking about or anything. Sure, it only has a handful of items on it, and most of those were added while writing this post.
